verses.commentary: Precisely dated: second year of Darius (520 BC), first day of sixth month. Haggai addresses both political (Zerubbabel) and religious (Joshua) leaders. God works through existing structures. Dual leadership models shared responsibility.

'These people' (not 'my people') suggests distance. The excuse: wrong time to rebuild the temple. Seventeen years since the return from exile. Priorities had drifted. Spiritual work perpetually postponed.
The word of the Lord comes again. Divine persistence. God does not abandon his purposes when his people delay. He sends another word.

Paneled houses while God's house lies ruined. The contrast stings. 'Paneled' (saphan) suggests luxury, perhaps cedar paneling like Solomon's palace. Self indulgence amid sacred neglect. Priorities exposed.
Give careful thought to your ways. Literally 'set your heart on your roads.' Self examination commanded. The phrase repeats twice in this chapter. Reflection precedes reformation.

Paradox of diminishing returns. Plant much, harvest little. Eat without satisfaction. Drink without filling. Clothe without warmth. Earn into a bag with holes. Effort produces no result. Futility signals divine displeasure.
Give careful thought again. The repeated command frames verses 5 through 7. Bracket structure emphasizes the middle content. Economic frustration points to spiritual cause.
Action commanded: go to mountains, get timber, build the house. God wants his dwelling place restored. Pleasure (ratsah) and honor (kabod) will result. Divine delight in completed obedience.

Expected much, got little. What you brought home, God blew away. The verb (naphach) means to breathe or blow, as if God exhales and possessions scatter. Each busy with his own house while God's remains ruined.
Therefore connects behavior to consequence. Heavens withhold dew, earth withholds crops. Covenant curses from Deuteronomy activated. Creation itself responds to covenant fidelity.
God claims responsibility for the drought. Called upon fields, mountains, grain, wine, oil, all produce, people, livestock, and all labor. Comprehensive judgment. Nothing escapes the divine summons.
Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the remnant obey. They fear the Lord. Rare prophetic success. The message works. Hearts turn. Fear of God produces faithful action.
Haggai now called 'the Lord's messenger' (malak), language typically reserved for angels. His message: 'I am with you.' Four words that change everything. Divine presence promised to obedient people.
The Lord stirred up spirits. Governor, priest, and all the people moved. Divine initiative awakens human response. They begin work on the temple. Action follows assurance.
Twenty fourth day of the sixth month, second year of Darius. Twenty three days from the first oracle. Remarkably quick response. The people moved from hearing to doing in less than a month.
